Let \( a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots \) be the unique sequence of nonnegative integers less than 397 with \( a_0 = 1 \) and

\[ a_{n+1}(a_n + 1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397} \]

for all nonnegative integers \( n \). Given that \( a_{2026} = 9 \), compute the remainder when \( a_0 + a_1 + \cdots + a_{2026} \) is divided by 397.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let all congruences be modulo \(397\). Since \(397\) is prime, nonzero residues are invertible.

Because \(a_{2026}=9\), no term \(a_0,\dots,a_{2026}\) is \(0\); otherwise once \(a_k=0\), all later terms would remain \(0\). Also, no relevant term is \(-1\), since then the recurrence would have no solution.

Define

\[
x_n \equiv a_n^{-1}.
\]

From the recurrence,

\[
a_{n+1}(a_n+1)^2 \equiv a_n,
\]

so, since \(a_n+1\) and \(a_n\) are invertible,

\[
a_{n+1} \equiv a_n(a_n+1)^{-2}.
\]

Taking reciprocals gives

\[
x_{n+1} \equiv (a_n+1)^2a_n^{-1}
= a_n+2+a_n^{-1}
= x_n+2+x_n^{-1}.
\]

Thus

\[
x_{n+1}-x_n \equiv 2+x_n^{-1}=2+a_n,
\]

so

\[
a_n \equiv x_{n+1}-x_n-2.
\]

Summing from \(n=0\) to \(2026\),

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv x_{2027}-x_0-2\cdot 2027.
\]

Since \(a_0=1\), we have \(x_0=1\). Also \(a_{2026}=9\), so

\[
x_{2026}=9^{-1}.
\]

Then

\[
x_{2027}=x_{2026}+2+x_{2026}^{-1}
=9^{-1}+2+9
=11+9^{-1}.
\]

Now

\[
9\cdot 44=396\equiv -1 \pmod{397},
\]

so

\[
9^{-1}\equiv -44\equiv 353 \pmod{397}.
\]

Therefore

\[
x_{2027}\equiv 11+353=364.
\]

Hence

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv 364-1-4054.
\]

Since \(4054\equiv 84\pmod{397}\),

\[
364-1-84=279.
\]

Thus the required remainder is

\[
\boxed{279}
\]
